```{r helpers}
species_code <- c("Homo sapiens" = "human", "Mus musculus" = "mouse", "Rattus norvegicus" = "rat")
sig_species <- function(g) if (mean(g == toupper(g)) > 0.8) "human" else "mouse"

sig_to_human <- function(genes) {
  if (sig_species(genes) == "human") return(unique(genes))
  o <- orthologs(genes, species = "mouse", human = FALSE)
  map <- setNames(o$human_symbol, o$symbol)
  h <- unname(map[genes]); h[is.na(h)] <- toupper(genes[is.na(h)])   # e.g. E2F1 written in human case
  unique(h)
}

collapse_dup_rows <- function(m, new_names) {
  ok <- !is.na(new_names) & new_names != ""
  m <- m[ok, , drop = FALSE]; new_names <- new_names[ok]
  o <- order(rowMeans(m), decreasing = TRUE); m <- m[o, , drop = FALSE]; new_names <- new_names[o]
  keep <- !duplicated(new_names); out <- m[keep, , drop = FALSE]; rownames(out) <- new_names[keep]; out
}

.cache <- new.env()
load_ds <- function(d, space) {
  key <- paste(d$file, space)
  if (!is.null(.cache[[key]])) return(.cache[[key]])
  e <- fread(file.path(PROJECT_DIR, "data", "processed", d$group, paste0(d$file, "_expr.csv.gz")), data.table = FALSE)
  m <- as.matrix(e[, -1]); rownames(m) <- e$gene
  p <- read.csv(file.path(PROJECT_DIR, "data", "processed", d$group, paste0(d$file, "_pheno.csv")),
                stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  sp <- index$species[index$dataset == d$file]
  if (space == "human" && sp != "Homo sapiens") {
    # numeric-only names (Entrez IDs used as placeholders, e.g. "100043387") make babelgene
    # treat the whole query as IDs and return nothing, so they are left out of the lookup
    keys <- rownames(m)[!grepl("^[0-9]+$", rownames(m))]
    o <- orthologs(keys, species = species_code[[sp]], human = FALSE)
    map <- setNames(o$human_symbol, o$symbol)
    m <- collapse_dup_rows(m, unname(map[rownames(m)]))
  }
  m <- m[apply(m, 1, var) > 0, , drop = FALSE]
  out <- list(expr = m, pheno = p, species = sp)
  .cache[[key]] <- out; out
}

score_sets <- function(m, genes) {
  g <- intersect(genes, rownames(m)); gs <- list(sig = g)
  empty <- setNames(as.data.frame(matrix(NA_real_, ncol(m), length(ALGS))), ALGS)
  if (length(g) < 2) return(list(scores = empty, n = length(g)))
  run <- function(param) as.numeric(gsva(param, verbose = FALSE)[1, ])
  s <- data.frame(GSVA   = run(gsvaParam(m, gs, kcdf = "Gaussian")),
                  ssGSEA = run(ssgseaParam(m, gs)),
                  PLAGE  = run(plageParam(m, gs)),
                  zScore = run(zscoreParam(m, gs)),
                  singscore = simpleScore(rankGenes(m), upSet = g)$TotalScore)
  # PLAGE is the first singular vector, whose sign is arbitrary per dataset: orient it
  # (without labels) so that it correlates positively with the zScore of the same genes
  if (isTRUE(cor(s$PLAGE, s$zScore) < 0)) s$PLAGE <- -s$PLAGE
  list(scores = s, n = length(g))
}

zfit   <- function(x) list(mu = colMeans(x), sd = pmax(apply(x, 2, sd), 1e-8))
zapply <- function(x, z) sweep(sweep(x, 2, z$mu, "-"), 2, z$sd, "/")

safe_auc <- function(y, pred, direction = "<") {
  if (length(unique(y[!is.na(pred)])) < 2) return(NULL)
  roc(y, pred, levels = c(0, 1), direction = direction, quiet = TRUE)
}
auc_row <- function(r, dataset, role, method, pred = NULL, y = NULL) {
  if (is.null(r)) return(NULL)
  ci <- tryCatch(as.numeric(ci.auc(r, method = "delong")), error = function(e) c(NA, NA, NA))
  acc <- if (!is.null(pred)) mean((pred >= 0.5) == (y == 1)) else NA
  data.frame(dataset = dataset, role = role, method = method, AUC = as.numeric(auc(r)),
             CI_low = max(0, ci[1]), CI_high = min(1, ci[3]), accuracy = acc,
             n_case = sum(y == 1), n_control = sum(y == 0))
}
roc_df <- function(r, dataset, method, auc_val) {
  if (is.null(r)) return(NULL)
  data.frame(fpr = 1 - r$specificities, tpr = r$sensitivities, dataset = dataset,
             method = method, AUC = auc_val)[order(1 - r$specificities, r$sensitivities), ]
}

# Class-balanced fitting. Without it, leave-one-out AUC is biased downwards: holding out a
# case leaves fewer cases in the fold, so the intercept (LR) or the vote share (RF)
# predicts a lower case probability for exactly the held-out cases, which can drive the
# pooled LOOCV AUC of an uninformative score towards 0 instead of 0.5.
fit_lr <- function(s, y) {
  w <- ifelse(y == 1, 0.5 / sum(y == 1), 0.5 / sum(y == 0)) * length(y)   # both classes weigh equally
  suppressWarnings(glm(y ~ s, family = binomial, data = data.frame(s = s, y = y), weights = w))
}
pred_lr <- function(fit, s) suppressWarnings(predict(fit, data.frame(s = s), type = "response"))
fit_rf <- function(x, y, seed = 2026) {
  set.seed(seed); f <- factor(y, levels = c(0, 1)); k <- min(table(f))
  randomForest(x, f, ntree = 500, strata = f, sampsize = c(k, k))      # balanced bootstrap per tree
}
pred_rf <- function(fit, x) predict(fit, x, type = "prob")[, "1"]

# Leave-pair-out AUC: hold out one case and one control together, refit on the rest, and
# score whether the case is ranked above the control. Nearly unbiased for small n.
lpo_auc <- function(X, y, fit_pred) {
  cases <- which(y == 1); ctrls <- which(y == 0); wins <- 0; k <- 0
  for (i in cases) for (j in ctrls) {
    tr <- setdiff(seq_along(y), c(i, j)); if (length(unique(y[tr])) < 2) next
    p <- fit_pred(X[tr, , drop = FALSE], y[tr], X[c(i, j), , drop = FALSE])
    wins <- wins + (p[1] > p[2]) + 0.5 * (p[1] == p[2]); k <- k + 1
  }
  if (k == 0) NA else wins / k
}
lr_fit_pred <- function(Xtr, ytr, Xte) { z <- zfit(Xtr); pred_lr(fit_lr(zapply(Xtr, z)[, 1], ytr), zapply(Xte, z)[, 1]) }
rf_fit_pred <- function(Xtr, ytr, Xte) { z <- zfit(Xtr); pred_rf(fit_rf(zapply(Xtr, z), ytr), zapply(Xte, z)) }
lpo_row <- function(auc, dataset, model, algorithm, y) data.frame(dataset = dataset, role = "Internal (leave-pair-out)",
  method = model_label(model, algorithm), AUC = auc, CI_low = NA, CI_high = NA, accuracy = NA,
  n_case = sum(y == 1), n_control = sum(y == 0), model = model, algorithm = algorithm)

binary_anova <- function(df, covar, score) {
  df <- df[!is.na(df$y) & !is.na(df[[score]]), ]
  covar <- covar[vapply(covar, function(cv) length(unique(df[[cv]])) > 1, TRUE)]
  rhs <- paste(c(covar, "factor(y)"), collapse = " + ")     # group entered last = adjusted for covariates
  a <- tryCatch(summary(aov(as.formula(paste0("`", score, "` ~ ", rhs)), data = df))[[1]], error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(a) || !"factor(y)" %in% trimws(rownames(a))) return(c(F = NA, p = NA))
  r <- a[trimws(rownames(a)) == "factor(y)", ]; c(F = r[["F value"]], p = r[["Pr(>F)"]])
}
oneway_anova <- function(df, score) {
  if (length(unique(df$condition)) < 2 || all(is.na(df[[score]]))) return(c(F = NA, p = NA))
  a <- summary(aov(as.formula(paste0("`", score, "` ~ condition")), data = df))[[1]]
  c(F = a[1, "F value"], p = a[1, "Pr(>F)"])
}

# Remove known study covariates (genotype, batch, LPS, sex, ...) from scores and gene values
# before classification. Uses design factors only, never the case/control labels; without it,
# a strong covariate that is balanced across groups can make held-out samples systematically
# mis-ranked and pushes cross-validated AUC towards 0.
usable_covar <- function(df, covar) covar[vapply(covar, function(cv) length(unique(df[[cv]])) > 1, TRUE)]
adjust_scores <- function(df, covar) {
  covar <- usable_covar(df, covar); if (!length(covar)) return(df)
  f <- as.formula(paste("s ~", paste(covar, collapse = " + ")))
  for (a in ALGS) if (!all(is.na(df[[a]]))) {
    s <- df[[a]]; df[[a]] <- resid(lm(f, data = cbind(df, s = s))) + mean(s)
  }
  df
}
adjust_expr <- function(m, pheno, covar) {
  covar <- usable_covar(pheno, covar); if (!length(covar) || !nrow(m)) return(m)
  mm <- model.matrix(as.formula(paste("~", paste(covar, collapse = " + "))), data = pheno)[, -1, drop = FALSE]
  limma::removeBatchEffect(m, covariates = mm)
}

# ---- Main validation routine -------------------------------------------------------
validate_signature <- function(sig_name, panel, train_id) {
  raw <- NutSignatures[[sig_name]]
  genes <- if (panel$space == "human") sig_to_human(raw) else unique(raw)
  ds <- setNames(panel$datasets, vapply(panel$datasets, `[[`, "", "id"))
  dat <- list(); datm <- list(); cover <- list(); expr <- list()
  for (d in ds) {
    L <- load_ds(d, panel$space)
    sc <- score_sets(L$expr, genes)
    p <- L$pheno
    y <- ifelse(p$condition %in% d$case, 1, ifelse(p$condition %in% d$control, 0, NA))
    dat[[d$id]] <- data.frame(dataset = d$label, id = d$id, p, y = y, sc$scores, check.names = FALSE)
    cover[[d$id]] <- data.frame(dataset = d$label, species = L$species, genes_in_signature = length(genes),
                                genes_found = sc$n, coverage = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * sc$n / length(genes)))
    datm[[d$id]] <- adjust_scores(dat[[d$id]], d$covar)                       # for models
    sg <- intersect(genes, rownames(L$expr))
    expr[[d$id]] <- adjust_expr(L$expr[sg, p$sample, drop = FALSE], p, d$covar)   # signature genes, for RF
  }

  # ANOVA for every dataset x scoring algorithm
  anova_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(ds, function(d) do.call(rbind, lapply(ALGS, function(a) {
    df <- dat[[d$id]]; ow <- oneway_anova(df, a); bn <- binary_anova(df, d$covar, a)
    data.frame(dataset = d$label, role = ifelse(d$id == train_id, "Training", "External"), algorithm = a,
               arms = length(unique(df$condition)), F_all_arms = ow[["F"]], p_all_arms = ow[["p"]],
               adjusted_for = if (length(d$covar)) paste(d$covar, collapse = ", ") else "—",
               F_case_vs_control = bn[["F"]], p_case_vs_control = bn[["p"]])
  }))))

  # Training data
  T  <- datm[[train_id]]; Tb <- T[!is.na(T$y), ]; n <- nrow(Tb)
  XT <- t(expr[[train_id]][intersect(genes, rownames(expr[[train_id]])), Tb$sample, drop = FALSE])
  XT <- XT[, apply(XT, 2, var) > 0, drop = FALSE]
  metrics <- list(); rocs <- list()
  add <- function(r, label, role, model, algorithm, pred = NULL, y = NULL, plot = TRUE) {
    row <- auc_row(r, label, role, model_label(model, algorithm), pred, y)
    if (is.null(row)) return(invisible())
    row$model <- model; row$algorithm <- algorithm
    metrics[[length(metrics) + 1]] <<- row
    if (plot) rocs[[length(rocs) + 1]] <<- roc_df(r, label, row$method, row$AUC)
  }
  directions <- c(); lr_full <- list()
  train_lab <- ds[[train_id]]$label

  for (a in ALGS) {
    s <- Tb[[a]]
    if (all(is.na(s))) next
    up <- mean(s[Tb$y == 1]) > mean(s[Tb$y == 0]); directions[a] <- if (up) "higher in case" else "lower in case"
    # in-sample score AUC (table only)
    add(safe_auc(Tb$y, s, if (up) "<" else ">"), train_lab, "Internal (LOOCV)", "Score", a, y = Tb$y, plot = FALSE)
    # logistic regression, leave-one-out (z-scoring refitted inside each fold)
    cv <- rep(NA_real_, n)
    for (i in seq_len(n)) {
      tr <- setdiff(seq_len(n), i); if (length(unique(Tb$y[tr])) < 2) next
      zs <- zfit(matrix(s[tr]))
      cv[i] <- pred_lr(fit_lr(zapply(matrix(s[tr]), zs)[, 1], Tb$y[tr]), zapply(matrix(s[i]), zs)[, 1])
    }
    add(safe_auc(Tb$y, cv), train_lab, "Internal (LOOCV)", "Logistic regression", a, cv, Tb$y)
    metrics[[length(metrics) + 1]] <- lpo_row(lpo_auc(matrix(s), Tb$y, lr_fit_pred), train_lab, "Logistic regression", a, Tb$y)
    lr_full[[a]] <- fit_lr(as.numeric(scale(s)), Tb$y)
  }

  # random forest on signature genes, leave-one-out
  rf_full <- NULL; imp <- NULL
  if (ncol(XT) >= 2) {
    cv <- rep(NA_real_, n)
    for (i in seq_len(n)) {
      tr <- setdiff(seq_len(n), i); if (length(unique(Tb$y[tr])) < 2) next
      zx <- zfit(XT[tr, , drop = FALSE])
      cv[i] <- pred_rf(fit_rf(zapply(XT[tr, , drop = FALSE], zx), Tb$y[tr]), zapply(XT[i, , drop = FALSE], zx))
    }
    add(safe_auc(Tb$y, cv), train_lab, "Internal (LOOCV)", "Random forest", "genes", cv, Tb$y)
    metrics[[length(metrics) + 1]] <- lpo_row(lpo_auc(XT, Tb$y, rf_fit_pred), train_lab, "Random forest", "genes", Tb$y)
    rf_full <- fit_rf(zapply(XT, zfit(XT)), Tb$y)
    imp <- data.frame(gene = rownames(importance(rf_full)), MeanDecreaseGini = importance(rf_full)[, 1])
  }

  # External: frozen models; each external dataset is z-scored on its own samples (no labels)
  for (d in ds) {
    if (d$id == train_id) next
    Eb <- datm[[d$id]]; Eb <- Eb[!is.na(Eb$y), ]
    if (length(unique(Eb$y)) < 2) next
    for (a in names(lr_full)) {
      if (all(is.na(Eb[[a]]))) next
      add(safe_auc(Eb$y, Eb[[a]], if (directions[a] == "higher in case") "<" else ">"),
          d$label, "External", "Score", a, y = Eb$y, plot = FALSE)
      pe <- pred_lr(lr_full[[a]], as.numeric(scale(Eb[[a]])))
      add(safe_auc(Eb$y, pe), d$label, "External", "Logistic regression", a, pe, Eb$y)
    }
    common <- intersect(colnames(XT), rownames(expr[[d$id]]))
    if (length(common) >= 2) {
      XE <- t(expr[[d$id]][common, Eb$sample, drop = FALSE])
      keep <- apply(XE, 2, var) > 0; common <- common[keep]; XE <- XE[, keep, drop = FALSE]
      if (length(common) >= 2) {
        rf_e <- fit_rf(zapply(XT[, common, drop = FALSE], zfit(XT[, common, drop = FALSE])), Tb$y)
        pr <- pred_rf(rf_e, zapply(XE, zfit(XE)))
        add(safe_auc(Eb$y, pr), d$label, "External", "Random forest", "genes", pr, Eb$y)
      }
    }
  }
  list(signature = sig_name, train = train_lab, directions = directions,
       scores = do.call(rbind, lapply(dat, function(x) x[, c("dataset", "id", "sample", "condition", "y", ALGS)])),
       coverage = do.call(rbind, cover), anova = anova_tab,
       metrics = do.call(rbind, metrics), rocs = do.call(rbind, rocs), importance = imp,
       labels = setNames(vapply(ds, `[[`, "", "label"), names(ds)))
}
```

```{r run-all}
results <- list()
for (pn in names(panels)) for (sg in names(panels[[pn]]$signatures)) {
  r <- validate_signature(sg, panels[[pn]], panels[[pn]]$signatures[[sg]])
  r$panel <- pn; results[[sg]] <- r
}
all_metrics <- do.call(rbind, lapply(results, function(r) if (!is.null(r$metrics)) cbind(signature = r$signature, panel = r$panel, r$metrics)))
not_scorable <- names(results)[vapply(results, function(r) is.null(r$metrics), TRUE)]
all_anova   <- do.call(rbind, lapply(results, function(r) cbind(signature = r$signature, panel = r$panel, r$anova)))
all_scores  <- do.call(rbind, lapply(results, function(r) cbind(signature = r$signature, r$scores)))
fwrite(all_metrics, file.path(RESULTS_DIR, "auc_summary.csv"))
fwrite(all_anova,   file.path(RESULTS_DIR, "anova_summary.csv"))
fwrite(all_scores,  file.path(RESULTS_DIR, "signature_scores.csv.gz"))
```

# Overview

This report tests whether each nutrition signature in `Signatures/NutSignaturesList.R`
separates **low-nutrient** samples from **replete or nutrient-treated** samples in the
public datasets downloaded by `Scripts/download_cnp_source_data.R` and processed by
`Scripts/process_cnp_source_data.R`.

* **`r length(tested)` of `r length(NutSignatures)` signatures** could be tested across
  **`r nrow(index)` processed datasets** (`r length(unique(unlist(lapply(panels, function(p) vapply(p$datasets, "[[", "", "id")))))` case/control contrasts).
* **Could not be scored:** `r if (length(not_scorable)) paste0(paste(not_scorable, collapse = ", "), " (fewer than two signature genes in the training data)") else "none"`.
* **Not testable with the current data (`r length(untested)`):** `r paste(untested, collapse = ", ")` —
  no downloaded expression dataset contrasts these nutrients.

Signatures come from two places: the **curated** list (`Signatures/NutSignaturesList.R`, not
modified) and **candidate** lists in `Signatures/CNP_Candidate_Signatures.csv`, produced by
`Scripts/derive_candidate_signatures.R` to fill gaps (GWAS-based vitamin E, vitamin K and carnitine
lists; a symbol-corrected vitamin E list; vitamin K lists re-derived from GSE148011). Each
signature's section states its source.

## Methods in brief

| Step | What is done |
|---|---|
| Expression | Log2 scale per dataset (log2 CPM for counts, log2(x+1) for FPKM/TPM, log2 intensity for arrays). Mouse/rat genes are mapped to human orthologs (babelgene) whenever a signature is tested across species; Vitamin K and Omega-3 are scored in their native species. |
| Signature scores | Five per-sample scores on all genes of each dataset: **GSVA**, **ssGSEA**, **PLAGE** and **zScore** (GSVA package `r packageVersion("GSVA")`, the implementations TBSignatureProfiler calls), plus **singscore**. PLAGE is oriented (no labels used) to correlate positively with zScore, because its sign is otherwise arbitrary in each dataset. |
| ANOVA | For every scoring algorithm: (i) one-way ANOVA of the score across **all** study arms; (ii) case vs control with study covariates entered first (e.g. genotype, batch, donor), so the group effect is covariate-adjusted. |
| ROC / AUC | AUC with DeLong 95% CI. The direction of the score (higher or lower in deficiency) is learned on the training set and **kept fixed** for external sets. |
| Logistic regression | `case ~ z(score)`, fitted separately for each scoring algorithm. With one predictor its ranking equals the score's, so the external LR AUC equals the fixed-direction score AUC; LR adds calibrated probabilities (accuracy at p ≥ 0.5). |
| Random forest | 500 trees on z-scored expression of the signature genes, with a class-balanced bootstrap (equal cases and controls per tree). |
| Covariates in models | Before classification, known study covariates (the "Adjusted for" column — genotype, batch, LPS, sex, ...) are regressed out of each score and each signature gene within its dataset. This uses design factors only, never the labels. Boxplots and ANOVA use the unadjusted scores (ANOVA adjusts in the model). |
| Internal validation | Leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) on the training dataset, plus a leave-pair-out AUC (one case + one control held out together), which is the less biased internal AUC for small groups. LOOCV: each sample is predicted by models fitted to all other samples, including the z-scoring. Both models are class-balanced (LR weights each class equally) — without this, pooled leave-one-out AUC is biased towards 0 for weak signatures, because holding out a case shifts the class balance of the fold against that case. |
| External validation | Models fitted once on the full training set, then applied unchanged to every other dataset in the panel. Each external dataset is z-scored on its own samples (no labels used). Random forest uses the signature genes present in both datasets. |

**Case = low nutrient** throughout: deficient diet, untreated/vehicle cells, or the
no-supplement arm. For treatment studies (calcitriol, ATRA, vitamin K precursor), the
vehicle arm is the "case", so an AUC above 0.5 means the signature tracks nutrient
*exposure*, not necessarily clinical deficiency.

## Datasets and contrasts

```{r datasets-table}
ctab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(panels), function(pn) do.call(rbind, lapply(panels[[pn]]$datasets, function(d) {
  ix <- index[index$dataset == d$file, ]
  p <- read.csv(file.path(PROJECT_DIR, "data", "processed", d$group, paste0(d$file, "_pheno.csv")))
  data.frame(Panel = pn, Dataset = d$label, Species = ix$species, Platform = ix$platform, Units = ix$units,
             `Case (low)` = paste(d$case, collapse = " + "), `Control (replete)` = paste(d$control, collapse = " + "),
             n = sprintf("%d vs %d", sum(p$condition %in% d$case), sum(p$condition %in% d$control)),
             Covariates = if (length(d$covar)) paste(d$covar, collapse = ", ") else "—", check.names = FALSE)
}))))
kable(ctab, format = "html", row.names = FALSE) |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed", "hover"), font_size = 12) |>
  collapse_rows(columns = 1, valign = "top") |> scroll_box(width = "100%")
```

# Summary of predictive performance

```{r summary-heatmap, fig.height = 0.24 * nrow(distinct(filter(all_metrics, model != "Score"), signature, dataset, role)) + 2.5, fig.width = 11}
hm <- all_metrics |>
  filter(model != "Score") |>
  mutate(row = case_when(role == "Internal (LOOCV)" ~ paste0(dataset, "  [train, LOOCV]"),
                         role == "Internal (leave-pair-out)" ~ paste0(dataset, "  [train, leave-pair-out]"),
                         TRUE ~ dataset),
         order = match(role, c("Internal (LOOCV)", "Internal (leave-pair-out)", "External")),
         method = factor(method, levels = names(METHOD_COLS)),
         signature = factor(signature, levels = names(results)),
         label = ifelse(is.na(AUC), "", sprintf("%.2f", AUC)))
hm <- hm |> arrange(signature, order, dataset)
hm$row <- factor(paste(hm$signature, hm$row, sep = "::"), levels = rev(unique(paste(hm$signature, hm$row, sep = "::"))))
ggplot(hm, aes(method, row, fill = AUC)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = label), size = 2.9) +
  facet_grid(signature ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y", switch = "y") +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = function(x) sub("^.*::", "", x)) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2c7bb6", mid = "#f7f7f7", high = "#d7191c", midpoint = 0.5, limits = c(0, 1)) +
  scale_x_discrete(position = "top", labels = function(x) sub(" · ", "\n", x)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "AUC", title = "Validated AUC by signature, dataset and model",
       subtitle = "[train] rows = internal validation on the training dataset; other rows = external validation of the frozen model.\nAUC < 0.5 on an external set means the score moved in the opposite direction to the training set.") +
  theme(plot.title.position = "plot", panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8), axis.text.x = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold"),
        strip.placement = "outside", strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 1, size = 9),
        panel.spacing.y = unit(0.35, "lines"))
```

### Internal validation (leave-one-out AUC on the training dataset)

```{r summary-loocv}
wide <- function(df) df |> select(signature, method, AUC) |> mutate(AUC = round(AUC, 2)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = method, values_from = AUC) |>
  select(signature, any_of(names(METHOD_COLS)))
loo <- all_metrics |> filter(role == "Internal (LOOCV)", model != "Score")
lpo <- all_metrics |> filter(role == "Internal (leave-pair-out)")
loo_w <- wide(loo) |> left_join(distinct(loo, signature, panel, Training = dataset), by = "signature") |>
  relocate(panel, Training, .after = signature)
loo_w <- loo_w[match(intersect(names(results), loo_w$signature), loo_w$signature), ]
fwrite(loo_w, file.path(RESULTS_DIR, "summary_loocv_auc.csv"))
lpo_w <- wide(lpo); lpo_w <- lpo_w[match(loo_w$signature, lpo_w$signature), ]
fwrite(lpo_w, file.path(RESULTS_DIR, "summary_leave_pair_out_auc.csv"))
kable(loo_w, format = "html", row.names = FALSE, caption = "Leave-one-out (LOOCV) AUC") |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed", "hover"), font_size = 12) |> scroll_box(width = "100%")
```

```{r summary-lpo}
kable(lpo_w, format = "html", row.names = FALSE, caption = "Leave-pair-out AUC (bias-corrected internal estimate)") |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed", "hover"), font_size = 12) |>
  footnote(general = "Pooled leave-one-out AUC is biased downwards for weak signals and very small training sets (it can fall far below 0.5 when there is no signal). Leave-pair-out removes one case and one control together and is close to unbiased; where the two disagree, trust leave-pair-out.") |>
  scroll_box(width = "100%")
```

ext <- all_metrics |> filter(role == "External", model != "Score") |>

ext_w <- wide(ext) |> left_join(ext |> group_by(signature) |> summarise(`External sets` = max(n)), by = "signature")

  footnote(general = paste("Signatures with no external dataset are omitted:",

                           ". AUC 0.5 = chance; below 0.5 = the signature moves in the opposite direction to the training set.")) |>
  scroll_box(width = "100%")

# Caveats for interpreting these results

* **Circular training sets.** `A_Retinol_Quiles_20` was derived from GSE299530 and
  `A_Retinol_GLM_43` from GSE134933 kidney; `B12_Cobalamin` was built from the cblX
  study (GSE161763); `Vitamin_K` was derived from GSE148011. Their internal (LOOCV) AUCs re-use the discovery data and are
  optimistic — the external columns are the real test.
* **Vitamin_K was replaced (2026-11-04).** The previous 50-gene list came from
  `~/Downloads/vitK_GSE148011_raw_counts.csv`, which merged GSE148011's vitamin K and erastin
  arms across two gene annotations (45,323 vs 53,384 IDs): all 50 genes had **zero counts in
  every vitamin K-arm sample** and ~460,000 counts in the erastin arm, so the list captured the
  annotation mismatch, not vitamin K. The new `Vitamin_K` is the set of genes higher with the
  vitamin K precursor within the vitamin K arm only (`Scripts/derive_candidate_signatures.R`).
  That response is weak (no gene reaches 2-fold; top genes are cell-cycle genes; ~48% of genes
  have p < 0.1, suggesting a broad, possibly technical, shift), and the list was derived from
  the training set, so its internal AUC is circular — only the external columns test it.
  One vitamin K library (GSM4452216, 20 µM, replicate 2; ~20,000 reads) failed QC and was excluded.
* **Added datasets (2026-11-04) have their own limits.** GSE1063 is a ~590-gene cDNA array
  (symbols parsed from gene names), so most signatures barely overlap it. GSE344237 always gives
  L-carnitine together with resveratrol, and GSE272401 gives vitamins D and K together. GSE271941
  compares two folic-acid doses (moderate vs fortified), not deficiency. GSE139892 uses a
  B6-pathway inhibitor rather than a deficient diet. GSE237219 has only 2 controls.
* **GWAS-based candidates.** `Vitamin_K_GWAS` uses the GWAS Catalog's suggestive threshold
  (p ≤ 1e-5) because vitamin K measurement has no genome-wide significant hits. GWAS genes
  affect circulating nutrient levels; they need not change expression in nutrient-exposed tissue.
* **Small groups.** GSE161763 (3 vs 3), GSE99113 (2 vs 2), GSE190371 (2 vs 2),
  GSE134933 liver (3 vs 3) and GSE104164 (3 vs 4) give very wide confidence intervals;
  an AUC of 1.0 on four samples is weak evidence.
* **Deficiency vs. treatment.** The vitamin D, ATRA and vitamin K contrasts compare
  vehicle with pharmacological doses of the active compound in cell culture, which is
  not the same biology as dietary deficiency in vivo.
* **Cross-species mapping.** Rodent datasets are scored on human orthologs; mouse-only
  genes (e.g. most `Gm*` and `*Rik` genes in `Vitamin_K` and `A_Retinol_GLM_43`) have no
  ortholog and drop out (see each coverage table).
* **External calibration.** Each external dataset is z-scored on its own samples so that
  platforms are comparable. This uses no labels, but it assumes cases and controls are
  both present, so accuracy at the 0.5 threshold depends on each study's case/control mix.
  AUC is unaffected.
* **Excluded datasets.** GSE266352 (LAMN vs colorectal metastases), GSE124395 (liver cell
  atlas), GSE246328 (NASH diet), GSE296260 (ccRCC), GSE143307 (methylation) and
  GSE271214/GSE271249 (RA-treated hESC, 2 per arm) have no usable nutrient contrast for
  expression-signature validation and were not processed.
